channel.description: Personally scored technology & science articles curated by news-filter

item.title: Microsoft patches Outlook security flaw; users urged to update
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Microsoft just patched a serious Outlook flaw. Time to update!
Microsoft has patched a security flaw in Outlook designated as CVE-2026-124194. The vulnerability allows attackers to trick users into opening a tampered message file, potentially enabling unauthorized server connections and credential theft. Microsoft classifies the issue as moderately severe but confirms active exploitation. Affected products include Microsoft 365 for business, Office LTSC 2021, and 2024. Tenable reports 1,093 vulnerabilities addressed in November updates, with 63 labeled critical. CISA added the flaw to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities. Microsoft recommends installing updates released on November 10th via account settings or IT departments for business users. The vulnerability requires user action to exploit.

item.title: Google updates Home app to address Nest camera issues and improve Gemini
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google's latest Home update fixes Nest camera headaches and upgrades Gemini
Google is rolling out updates to its Google Home app and Gemini AI, addressing Nest camera issues and enhancing smart home functionality. The Gemini improvements include better handling of complex commands by asking follow-up questions to clarify device intent, visual responses on smart displays, faster timer and alarm controls, and conversational voice feedback. The Google Home app fixes camera problems for older Nest devices, resolving live-streaming issues with models like Nest Cam Indoor, Outdoor, and Doorbell. Updates also address network setups like PPPoE and fiber internet, restoring event thumbnails and improving clock accuracy for Nest Cam IQ. Android users receive fixes for camera history controls and reduced account-linking prompts. Additional features include Eco Mode for thermostats, digital home keys via Google Wallet, and expanded AI agents for managing appliances, EV chargers, and more. Users are advised to update devices via the Google Home app to access these changes.

item.title: United Airlines Blocks AI Booking Agents Over Security Risks
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends, PCMag Original headline: United Airlines Restricts AI Agents from Booking Flights Over Security and Regulatory Concerns
United Airlines has blocked third-party AI agents from completing flight bookings, citing security risks and regulatory concerns. The airline joins JPMorgan Chase and Amazon in restricting AI access to services, per The Wall Street Journal. United warns AI agents could expose customer data, enable unintended purchases, or alter loyalty program benefits. The move may violate Department of Transportation and Federal Aviation Administration rules requiring human verification for baggage compliance checks. CEO Scott Kirby expressed reluctance to adopt agentic commerce, stating, 'I don’t want to create another middleman.' Southwest integrates ChatGPT for flight searches, while Delta allows authenticated AI assistants with safeguards. The decision affects customers, travel agencies, and aggregators, as Bloomberg notes an FTC inquiry into potential AI-driven pricing adjustments. AI tools can display flight options and fares but cannot finalize bookings. Engadget highlights limited agentic commerce, with Uber reporting only four AI-driven rides among 320 million trips. United supports AI for research but insists on 'established protections' for travelers before deeper integration. The move reflects industry caution balancing innovation with security and compliance.

item.title: TSMC invests $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
TSMC's board approved a $1 billion investment in Anthropic and OpenAI, allocating $500 million to OpenAI preferred stock and $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at its expected IPO price. The move grants TSMC direct stakes in leading AI developers amid its own success in AI data center chip manufacturing. Analysts noted that circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers complicates assessing real market demand for AI hardware and services. TSMC produces most of Nvidia’s AI chips and Apple’s custom chips for devices and servers, with fabrication plants in Taiwan, Japan, China, and Arizona, and a new German facility under construction.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Resigns Over Affairs and Alleged Spy Ties
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Digital Trends, Latest from TechRadar US in News, The Verge, Ars Technica, PCMag Original headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandal Over Affairs and Alleged Spy Ties
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after admitting to multiple extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a Chinese executive alleged to be a spy, and another with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare. The board accepted his resignation effective immediately, appointing CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Huang’s 33-year tenure ended as the company’s stock dropped over 10% pre-market, losing more than $400 billion in value. The FBI is investigating whether his relationships compromised national security, citing suspicions that Megaspeed facilitated the transfer of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms. The board launched an inquiry into the allegations, with some House Republicans threatening subpoenas if Huang does not cooperate. Kress, who has led financial operations for over a decade, will oversee the search for a permanent CEO, considering both internal and external candidates. The scandal has intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s ties to Chinese companies and raised questions about governance risks from concentrating power in one leader. The company faces challenges in recovering from the crisis while maintaining its leadership in AI and data center technologies.
item.source: TechCrunch, Digital Trends, Latest from TechRadar US in News, The Verge, Ars Technica, PCMag

item.title: Google Adds Gemini AI to Apple CarPlay for Voice Conversations
item.description:
Source: Engadget, PCMag Original headline: Google Expands Gemini AI Assistant to Apple CarPlay, Enabling Voice Conversations
Google has expanded its Gemini AI assistant to Apple CarPlay, enabling voice-based conversations through vehicle infotainment systems. The update, available today for supported Gemini Live languages, features a dedicated app interface on CarPlay, separate from its previous Google Maps integration. Users can access Gemini via a dedicated icon, with conversations syncing to the Gemini iPhone app and retaining chat history across devices. The integration follows enhancements to Gemini's Personal Assistance feature on Android Auto, which uses data from other Google apps for tailored responses. Gemini can now help users prepare for meetings, review emails, or receive daily briefings during commutes. Sample prompts include 'prep for a 10 a.m. meeting with the design team' or 'catch up on unread emails.' The assistant also offers dining recommendations and historical insights about landmarks. Setup requires updating the Gemini app, granting microphone permissions, and prior Gemini Live usage. Conversations are saved to chat history but are limited to voice mode on CarPlay, requiring users to start a 'New Conversation' from the infotainment screen. This marks another step in Google's strategy to integrate Gemini across platforms.

item.title: Hackers exploit AntiFox AI tool to steal AWS credentials
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: AntiFox AI agents hijacked by hackers to carry out theft of AWS credentials
Cybercriminals are using the open-source AI-powered pentesting tool AntiFox to steal Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials, according to security researchers at Arctic Wolf. The researchers found threat actors hosting AntiFox instances on Alibaba Cloud to analyze compromised systems, search for passwords, and access cloud resources. AntiFox, developed by a Chinese developer, is a fork of ARTEX, another AI-powered penetration testing framework linked to recent cyberattacks. Arctic Wolf observed attackers compromising Microsoft IIS servers, installing web shells to extract database credentials, and using stolen AWS keys to access internal resources. Amazon confirmed its services were not compromised but urged customers to secure credentials and follow best practices. Researchers recommend monitoring web servers for suspicious activity, restricting application permissions, enabling logging, and rotating exposed credentials. ARTEX, released in late 2026, was linked to attacks on South Korea’s financial sector and was later closed-source by its developer. Censys identified 1,465 hosts running ARTEX, with 10% also hosting other attack tools.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: NASA's Lunar Push Driven by Rapid Procurement Reforms
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: NASA's secret weapon in the lunar space race may be ... procurement reform?
NASA officials announced multiple lunar contracts and mission decisions during a news conference, emphasizing rapid procurement to advance the Artemis Moon Base program. Carlos García-Galán, manager of the Moon Base Program, noted the agency is keeping industry engaged with frequent solicitations to meet its timeline. The Artemis program represents NASA’s most credible effort to establish a permanent lunar outpost. Officials are collaborating with a broad range of U.S. commercial space companies, including those without prior orbital experience. Legal expert Mike Gold, formerly with NASA, described the procurement pace as unprecedented, with five lunar contracts issued in seven days. He highlighted the diverse involvement of large, small, new, and established companies. The approach underscores NASA’s focus on creative contracting strategies to accelerate lunar settlement efforts.

item.title: GENTO Debuts 21-DoF Hand at CoRL 2026, NVIDIA Launches GR00T 2
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: GENTO Debuts a 21-DoF Hand at CoRL 2026 as NVIDIA Launches GR00T 2 With TIANJI Marvin Pro
GENTO's 21-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand debuts at CoRL 2026, addressing four mechanical challenges: backlash, fragility, backdrivability, and fingertip force. The design uses high-precision linkage transmission, impact-resistant structures, and MIT hybrid control for compliant interaction. Tianji Intelligence showcases the hand alongside TIANJI Marvin Pro and GENTO Luna at Booth 602. NVIDIA's GR00T 2, demonstrated with TIANJI Marvin Pro, enables coordinated robot tasks using force data. The hardware includes MEMS torque sensors detecting 0.02 N·m with 160 Hz bandwidth and ±0.03 mm accuracy. Benchmark tests show tracking error reduced to 1.89 mm and latency to 5 ms. Tianji Intelligence, incubated by Yaskawa Electric and Everwin Precision, claims 2,000 force-controlled arms deployed in 2025. The company's data pipeline links VR, gloves, and teleoperation for real-world robot training, supporting AI models like Motus2. GENTO and TIANJI platforms aim to bridge digital AI policies with physical execution, with hardware available for testing at CoRL 2026.

item.title: Researchers Develop Full-Body Motion Tracking for Smartwatches Using Ultrasonic Tech
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Your smartwatch can already do full-body motion tracking. Researchers just unlocked it at zero cost on Wear OS.
Researchers at Cornell University’s SciFi Lab developed EchoMotion, a system using ultrasonic sound waves from a smartwatch’s speaker and microphone to track full-body motion without additional hardware. The AI-driven system, under 30MB, reconstructs body posture by analyzing echoes from the wearer’s limbs and torso. Tested on 10 participants, it achieved 95.4% accuracy in recognizing 20 gym exercises, with calibration reducing joint error from 4 inches to 2.4 inches. The tech works on unmodified Samsung Galaxy Watch 6, 7, and Google Pixel Watch 3, with minimal accuracy loss. It uses 12 milliwatts of power, 40 times less than a camera system, and functions in noisy environments like gyms. Potential applications include fitness feedback for Pilates and rehabilitation. The team notes EchoMotion’s compatibility with commercial devices could ease adoption. Saif Mahmud, lead researcher, emphasized the milestone for body tracking without custom hardware.

item.title: Prusa launches affordable ESD 3D printing filament for electronics manufacturing
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Prusa launches new carbon-fiber and carbon-nanotube-filled 3D printing filament for electronics manufacturing
Prusa introduced Prusament PETG ESD, a carbon-fiber and carbon-nanotube-filled filament designed for static-sensitive electronics. Priced at $56.99, it is cheaper than Prusa’s non-ESD PETG Carbon Fiber variant. The filament targets electronics production, such as PCB fixtures and IC trays, rather than hobbyist use. Prusa claims it improves dimensional accuracy and reduces warping compared to competitors’ ESD filaments, which range from $65.98 to $105. While non-ESD filaments are generally safe for enclosures, Prusa positions this product for manufacturing efficiency, reducing reliance on CNC-machined ESD trays. The company uses PETG ESD in its own production to prevent overcoating during powder coating. Prusa has not yet released a datasheet detailing strength metrics but notes increased stiffness and reduced toughness compared to standard PETG. It is the only ESD filament offering carbon fiber reinforcement, making it the most affordable option available.

item.title: Nintendo Ends Google and Apple Sign-In Support by 2027
item.description:
Source: Engadget, PCMag Original headline: Nintendo to Discontinue Google and Apple Sign-Ins by Early 2027
Nintendo will stop supporting Google and Apple sign-ins for Nintendo accounts starting January 26, 2027. Users will no longer be able to create new accounts or log in with third-party credentials. The My Nintendo Platinum Points program, which linked Google or Apple accounts to profiles, will also end. Nintendo urged users to switch to passwords or passkeys via the Accounts page. Existing users may face re-authentication prompts, requiring email/password or passkey logins. Credential recovery is possible through the Nintendo Account login page, though email access is needed for most cases. The change aligns with industry trends toward stronger account security and direct user management. Nintendo did not explain the reason for the shift, but emphasized preparing for the transition to avoid disruptions to gaming services.

item.title: Fireworks AI breach exposed Notion customers' chat data
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access Notion customers’ chat transcripts
Fireworks AI confirmed a cyberattack that exposed customer data, including Notion users' chat transcripts. Hackers breached Fireworks' cloud provider, accessing billing info and datasets. Notion disclosed the breach affected 1% of its customers after Fireworks alerted them. The company disconnected from Fireworks on November 3, deleted stored data, and halted connectivity. Notion confirmed hackers stole chat transcripts from its AI customers using the 'Insights' feature, though much of the data was unattributable. Fireworks claims attackers are financially motivated, targeting large language models to sell tokens. This is the second breach at Fireworks in two months, following an October incident.

item.title: Lego’s BrickLink marketplace offline for a week due to unusual activity
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Lego’s BrickLink marketplace has been offline for a week following ‘unusual activity’
Lego’s BrickLink marketplace has been offline since November 5th due to 'unusual activity.' The company took the site offline to secure the platform, protect users, and ensure data integrity. Lego has not provided a return date, stating it needs to fully investigate the issue and contain any related problems. Updates were previously expected by November 11th, but the latest statement indicates no estimate remains. This follows a similar incident in 2020 when a cybersecurity threat led to a temporary shutdown. At that time, users were prompted to change passwords, though accounts were not compromised. Lego has not disclosed specifics about the current incident, emphasizing its focus on resolving the issue before restoring service.

item.title: Slow Laptop Performance Could Be Battery-Related
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Your slow laptop might just have a battery problem
Laptop performance issues may stem from battery management settings or hardware. When unplugged, laptops often throttle performance to conserve power, especially in gaming models. Windows 11's 'Best power efficiency' mode prioritizes battery life over speed, potentially causing slowdowns. Users can switch to 'Balanced' or 'Best performance' modes to test improvements. Failing batteries can also impact performance, even when plugged in, as some systems use batteries to supplement power during heavy workloads. Dell's Hybrid Power technology exemplifies this. A significant drop in battery capacity, indicated by the 'Design Capacity' versus 'Full Charge Capacity' in Windows' battery report, may signal a need for replacement. Faulty chargers or underpowered adapters can also cause insufficient power delivery. Before discarding a laptop, checking battery health via the built-in 'powercfg /batteryreport' tool is recommended. If performance issues persist after addressing settings and hardware, contacting the manufacturer under warranty is advised.

item.title: Google Wallet Adds Digital House Keys After Years of Delay
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google Wallet finally gets digital house keys, years after Apple
Google has added digital home keys to Google Wallet, enabling Android users to unlock compatible smart locks via phone taps or proximity. Apple introduced similar functionality in 2021, and Samsung launched its version earlier this year. The feature is available through the Google Home Public Preview and will expand soon. Users can add digital keys to Wallet alongside payment cards and car keys. Two unlocking methods exist: NFC, which requires a phone near the lock and recent unlock, and UWB, which unlocks as users approach via manual setup. A single key can access multiple locks in a home, with additional keys available for other household members. NFC works on Android 9+ with Matter-certified locks like Aqara U400 and Schlage Sense Pro. UWB requires newer Pixel models. Wear OS watches aren't supported initially.

item.title: Xbox Launches Co-Op Horror Game 'Last Pirates: Die Together'
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Xbox just got a bizarre co-op horror game where pirates lose their butts
RetroStyle Games' Last Pirates: Die Together launched on Xbox Series X|S and PC via Game Preview on November 11. The co-op horror game features pirates navigating cursed islands, collecting treasure while avoiding monsters and traps. Players can lose their butts to revive teammates or play basketball with them. A Mimic monster copies players' appearance and voice chat. The $9.99 Game Preview version includes lobby browsers, weapons, and progression systems, with crossplay support for Steam and Xbox Play Anywhere. RetroStyle confirmed simultaneous updates for Xbox and Steam, with a full release planned for Q1 2027. The game initially debuted in Steam Early Access in January 2026 and reached 350,000 Steam wishlists. A demo ranked in Steam Next Fest's top 50.

item.title: Windows 11 Update Adds Faster Edge, Cloud Rebuild, and Accessibility Tweaks
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Windows 11 gets a faster File Explorer, easier recovery, and new accessibility features
Microsoft has rolled out the November 2026 update for Windows 11 (KB5132061), introducing performance and usability improvements. Microsoft Edge now launches faster and more reliably, even with background tasks. File Explorer's right-click menu is streamlined, with quicker access and customizable shortcuts. Xbox mode users benefit from an enhanced task view for switching between desktop and game sessions. The key feature, Cloud Rebuild, allows Windows 11 to restore a clean system image with correct drivers via Windows Update, eliminating the need for USB recovery tools. Accessibility upgrades include Magnifier enhancements, enabling dynamic contrast themes, per-monitor zoom, and frozen zoom areas. Microsoft also shared tips for improving readability, such as adjusting text size, scaling apps, quick zoom via keyboard shortcuts, and customizing cursor visibility. The update prioritizes refining the user experience over adding new features, with adjustments to text, scaling, and pointer settings helping personalize the interface.

item.title: CoreWeave shifts to prepayments and short-term contracts for AI growth
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
CoreWeave is shifting its financing strategy to rely on customer prepayments and short-term contracts to fund AI growth. The company reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% year-over-year, but posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense. CEO Michael Intrator said the company will not use unsecured debt at current yields, instead relying on loans backed by specific customer contracts. CoreWeave expects $9 billion in prepayments and deposits over three months, including $3 billion tied to new customer contracts for existing capacity. The firm raised prices 25% in July and 10% later in the quarter, with short-term deals commanding prices over $40 million per megawatt annually. A $2.6 billion loan, DDTL 5.5, was closed in August to fund short-term opportunities. Bond investors remain skeptical, with yields on CoreWeave’s bonds hitting above 15% recently. The strategy aims to boost profits but carries risks from contract renewals and pricing volatility.

item.title: Mozilla Removes 50GB Data Cap for Firefox Free VPN Temporarily
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Mozilla Temporarily Lifts 50GB Data Limit for Firefox's Free Built-In VPN
Mozilla is temporarily removing the 50GB monthly data limit for Firefox's free built-in VPN until January 31, 2027. The change, described as a 'holiday gift,' allows unlimited data usage for users. The VPN, introduced last year as a privacy feature to hide IP addresses, initially had a 50GB cap. Mozilla claims the uncapped limit is a 'gift' to users, though some suspect it may be a trial for future features. The company emphasizes it does not sell browsing data, track users, or log websites visited. The Firefox VPN uses Fastly's content delivery network, which states it does not log proxied request destinations or share connection metadata with Mozilla or third parties beyond abuse prevention needs.

item.title: Fractile Raises $720M to Advance AI Chip Development
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
Fractile, a British AI chip startup, raised $720 million in Series C funding led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, and others. The round, backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund, aims to boost the U.K.’s role in AI hardware development. The company’s valuation is reported at over £5 billion, possibly $7 billion. Fractile’s approach combines custom AI chip design with a machine learning compiler to optimize large model execution. Its hardware uses stacked DRAM to address memory-capacity trade-offs critical for agentic AI applications. CEO Walter Goodwin noted the funding will enable the company to deliver its first chips and systems next year. The investment positions Fractile as a top contender in the AI chip race, alongside firms like Axelera and OLIX, as demand grows for cost-effective inference solutions.

item.title: ByteDance is reportedly working on its own AI agent
item.description:
Source: Engadget
ByteDance is preparing an AI assistant to compete with Meta's Muse, Bloomberg reports. The AI agent, expected to be revealed soon, will serve a similar role to Muse, which has attracted over 10 million users. Meta's CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, has predicted the AI agent could generate more revenue per user than existing apps and will play a key role in Meta's AI glasses. It remains unclear if ByteDance plans to integrate the agent into hardware. The company's AI efforts, including its video generator Seedance, have faced legal scrutiny from U.S. studios. ByteDance cofounder Zhang Yiming told employees its AI initiatives may take until 2029 or 2030 to catch up with frontier AI companies. If launched, the AI agent could raise data privacy concerns about personal access. ByteDance did not immediately comment on the report.

item.title: Anduril satellite tracks spacecraft in Earth's shadow using infrared sensor
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night
Anduril Industries demonstrated its satellite Anduril-216, which tracks spacecraft in Earth’s shadow using a long-wave infrared sensor. The satellite, launched in July on a SpaceX rideshare mission, orbits 590 km above Earth, spending one-third of each orbit in darkness. Its infrared imager can detect objects in full dark, according to Gokul Subramanian, Anduril’s senior vice president of engineering. 'This is a unique sensor that allows us to take imagery in long-wave infrared. It has a huge dynamic range and very low solar exclusion,' he said. The Space Force relies on tracking satellites to monitor adversary movements and issue collision alerts. Adam Thurn, Anduril’s vice president, noted the gap in optical tracking during orbital night. 'We can’t see satellites not illuminated by the Sun,' he said. Anduril acquired ExoAnalytic Solutions to enhance satellite tracking capabilities. The sensor aims to close the gap in monitoring spacecraft maneuvers in Earth’s shadow.

item.title: Whoop launches social network for health data sharing
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Whoop just launched a social network
Whoop, the fitness band company, launched a social network called Whoop Humans within its app, allowing members to follow friends and share health data. The platform lets users choose what to share, from sleep to workouts, with opt-in privacy controls. CEO Will Ahmed emphasized the network's intimacy compared to existing Teams feature, which uses group leaderboards. Privacy measures include stealth mode, sensitive activity markers, and content reporting. Whoop is expanding into medical wellness with FDA-cleared features like ECG and blood pressure insights, and has seen "huge growth" among users over 60. The company is also preparing for an IPO and expanding retail sales through Ulta stores. Ahmed noted competition from Apple and Oura but stressed staying true to its "aspiring" user base. Whoop now has 1,200 employees, over 4 million members by year-end, and 70% annual membership growth.

item.title: Norwest launches $4B AI fund with global investment focus
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Norwest pushes deeper into AI with new $4B fund
Norwest, backed by Wells Fargo, has raised a $4 billion fund as part of its 18th investment vehicle and largest to date. The fund targets AI startups across sectors like consumer, healthcare, and technology, with investments in the U.S., India, and Israel. Jeff Crowe, senior managing partner, emphasized a broad AI strategy, stating the technology’s impact spans industries, geographies, and applications. Norwest plans to focus on early-stage companies developing AI-native applications, physical AI, domain-specific models, and cybersecurity solutions. Recent investments include Coval, which tests AI agents, and Generalist AI, which builds foundation models for robots. Since closing its $3 billion 17th fund in 2024, the firm has made over 87 investments. Crowe highlighted AI’s potential to transform enterprise, consumer, and healthcare solutions through widespread adoption.

item.title: Metalenz acquires HoloCoder tech to boost smartphone night photography
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: A new camera technology could dramatically improve how smartphones take photos at night
Metalenz acquired PxE Holographic Imaging to develop HoloCoder technology, which enhances smartphone night photography. The tech uses a microscopic optical layer to redirect light wavelengths toward sensor pixels, capturing up to 2.5 times more light than traditional Bayer filters. This could improve low-light performance, dynamic range, and 3D depth sensing without increasing sensor size. Current smartphone cameras lose 60% of incoming light via Bayer filters, leading to shadow noise and dynamic range issues. HoloCoder potentially eliminates the need for additional depth-sensing hardware. Metalenz plans to integrate the tech into consumer electronics by late 2027 or early 2028, though no smartphone manufacturers have confirmed adoption. The technology may also find applications in robotics and autonomous vehicles.

item.title: Former BioWare exec launches free mobile RPG with console-quality experience
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: This free RPG from a former BioWare exec's studio promises a console-quality experience — all on your phone
A new free-to-play mobile RPG, UnGodly, launched on Google Play. Developed by Azra Games, founded by former BioWare and EA executive Mark Otero, the game is a dark fantasy action RPG centered on a mercenary named Vander and his squad of divine warriors called Primals. Each Primal, descended from an ancient god, offers unique combat abilities, with over 20 unlockable characters including Conan the Barbarian via a crossover. Character progression features quests and relationships, with meaningful rewards for short play sessions. Otero claims the game delivers 'console-quality depth, fidelity, and experience' comparable to PC or console titles. Available on Google Play with PC controls via Google Play Games, it will expand to Samsung Galaxy Store and One Store next month. The game promises tens of hours of play without requiring extended sessions.

item.title: Ring confirms camera drone lacks manual controls after CBS crash
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Ring confirms its camera drone won’t have manual controls after crashing on CBS News
Ring’s Drone Cam will lack manual controls, relying solely on AI autopilot. During a CBS News demo, founder Jamie Siminoff allowed reporter Jo Ling Kent to manually fly an early version, resulting in two crashes. The first crash occurred when collision avoidance technology failed, though Ring declined to share pre-crash footage. The second crash happened after the drone lost internet connectivity, preventing it from landing as intended. Siminoff noted the drone was supposed to stop and land but did not. Ring declined to show the app and confirmed manual controls won’t be available at launch. A spokesperson, Sam McGee, stated autonomous flight with AI Pilot offers the best customer experience, though the decision wasn’t tied to the CBS demo. Manual controls were part of development but excluded from the final product.

item.title: IT leaders see AI's value but few have implemented it
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Leaders agree AI is vital for their workplace — but barely any are doing anything about it
A Lenovo report reveals that while 80% of IT leaders recognize AI's potential for the workplace, only 10% have implemented digital transformations to support it. The sixth volume of the Lenovo Work Reborn report, based on a 1,200-person survey across nine countries, highlights a growing 'AI readiness divide.' Organizations struggle with governance, ROI measurement, and workflow redesign. Just 10% have AI governance frameworks, and fewer measure AI's impact. The AI Workplace Readiness Index scores range from 2.7 for early-stage adopters to 4.1 for fully integrated businesses. Rakshit Ghura, Lenovo's Vice President, stresses the need for measurable value, such as reduced cycle times and improved outcomes, to justify AI investments. He warns that outdated workplaces hinder AI effectiveness, urging leaders to redesign workflows with proper governance and support.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Meta's Infrastructure Head Steps Down, New Leader Named
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Meta is losing its longtime head of infrastructure
Santosh Janardhan, Meta's longtime head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, is stepping down. He will be replaced by Dave Brown, who joined Meta as vice president of infrastructure earlier this year. Brown previously spent 19 years at Amazon focusing on compute, cloud, and AI. Janardhan will remain at Meta through 2024 in an advisory role for Meta Compute, the company's initiative to scale data center investments. Bloomberg first reported his departure, citing an internal memo that did not specify reasons. The memo referenced the need to 'pass the baton,' though Meta did not confirm details. The company has significantly expanded its infrastructure investments in recent years to compete in the AI race, with Janardhan leading Meta Compute efforts earlier this year.

item.title: Old Power Banks Should Be Recycled, Not Thrown Away
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Don't toss that old power bank in the trash — here's where it actually goes
Old power banks should be recycled, not thrown away. Lithium-ion batteries in power banks are flammable and pose fire risks if discarded in regular trash. Disposal methods vary by state, with some allowing lithium-ion batteries in regular waste and others requiring specialized recycling. Residents should check local government websites or contact fire departments for disposal guidelines. Recycling centers and hardware stores like Lowe's and Home Depot often partner with organizations like Call2Recycle for battery disposal. Power banks with swelling, overheating, or charge retention issues should be discarded immediately. Certified power banks with logos like CCC, FCC, or UL 2056 are safer options. Unverified claims like 'TSA-approved' lack official certification. Proper disposal prevents fire hazards and reduces e-waste.

item.title: Mass Effect Composer Warns AI Can't Replace Human Creativity in Games
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: ‘AI is not an artist’ — Mass Effect 1 and 2 composer shares his stance on AI replacement in video games, says ‘Machines can never be artists as they aren’t human’
Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 composer Jack Wall warns against AI replacing human creativity in video games. In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, Wall argues AI should not replace human artists but can serve as a 'creative tool' to aid the process. He states, 'AI is not an artist,' emphasizing machines lack human essence required for art. 'Machines can never be artists as they aren’t human,' he adds, noting art's purpose is human communication. Wall criticizes AI music for merely replicating past work rather than innovating. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 composer Jason Graves echoes similar concerns, calling AI incapable of replicating human emotional depth and creative inspiration. Both composers stress the irreplaceable value of human creativity in game development as AI integration grows in the industry.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Uber, DoorDash, Airbnb report minimal AI agent usage for bookings
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Hardly anyone is using AI agents for bookings, according to Uber and Airbnb
Uber, DoorDash, and Airbnb report minimal use of AI agents for bookings, with numbers far below human transaction volumes. Uber recorded 320 million human rides versus just four AI bookings in a week. DoorDash CEO Tony Xu noted hundreds of AI orders, a small fraction of its billions annually. Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky cited user preference for personal trip research over AI-driven bookings. Users criticized AI agents as tedious, with Reddit comments arguing they strip joy from mundane tasks. A user described AI agents as requiring more steps than using apps directly. Reports indicate AI tools may increase work hours and correction time. United Airlines and governments like Sweden have restricted AI agents. Experts suggest widespread adoption is unlikely soon, as not all tasks are suited for automation.

item.title: Olaf Sakkers Challenges Emerging-Manager Squeeze in VC
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Olaf Sakkers is betting he can beat the emerging-manager squeeze
Venture capital fundraising remains challenging for first-time managers, with PitchBook data showing firms raising fourth or later funds captured 88.2% of U.S. VC dollars in 2026’s first three quarters, while first-time funds secured just 4.5%. Olaf Sakkers, founder of RedBlue Capital, defied the trend by raising a second fund totaling $50 million. After studying anthropology and serving in the Israel Defense Forces, he joined Maniv Mobility as an analyst, later co-founding RedBlue. The firm focuses on robotics, logistics, and energy, using small checks and strategic introductions to gain trust. Sakkers cites strong returns, with 15 of 28 investments marked up and a net internal rate of return significantly above 50%. Backed companies like HappyRobot and Westmag achieved major funding rounds. He emphasizes discipline, using AI tools and a custom database to track relationships. Despite long exit timelines, Sakkers argues smaller funds outperform larger ones, and he remains undeterred by the competitive landscape. 'Life is short, and regrets last forever,' he says, reflecting his determination to succeed in venture capital.

item.title: Noctua launches space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad for AMD processors
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Noctua brings space-grade carbon nanotube thermal pad to AMD AM5 and AM4 processors
Noctua launched its NT-CP1 thermal pad for AMD AM4 and AM5 processors, using Carbice's carbon nanotube technology originally developed for aerospace. Priced at $24.95 in the US and €25.95 in Europe, the pad offers improved heat transfer performance that enhances over time rather than degrading. Unlike conventional thermal pastes, the NT-CP1 features an aluminum core with carbon nanotubes and a polymer coating for durability and electrical insulation. The pad's 90µm thickness and 33x33mm size fit both AM4 and AM5 sockets. Noctua claims the manufacturing process uses recycled aluminum and waste carbon gas, making it more energy-efficient than traditional graphite-based alternatives. CEO Roland Mossig highlighted the pad's ease of installation and long-term maintenance-free performance. The product is designed for users seeking consistent thermal efficiency without periodic replacements.

item.title: Maersk confirms data breach after hackers demand $5 million ransom
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Shipping giant Maersk confirms data breach as hackers demand $5 million ransom
Maersk confirmed a cyberattack on a legacy system from its acquired logistics company LF Logistics, with hackers demanding $5 million ransom. The ransomware group WhiteArmor claims to have stolen 100GB of data, including 30,000 driver records, plaintext passwords, 33 SUPER_ADMIN accounts, and mobile device logs. Maersk stated core operations remain unaffected and found no evidence of data exposure beyond the isolated system. The attackers threatened to leak the data if ransom isn't paid, citing LF Logistics' role in managing fulfillment for major brands. Maersk acquired LF Logistics in 2022 for $3.6 billion. WhiteArmor also claimed 27,842 mobile logs containing personal identifiers. The breach follows Maersk's 2017 NotPetya attack, which cost the company $250–$300 million. The company warns of potential phishing risks from exposed data but has not confirmed payment.

item.title: Roku ends smart home gadget production, refocuses on streaming
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Back to Streaming: Roku Stops Making Smart Home Gadgets
Roku is ending production of smart home gadgets after four years of expansion, refocusing on its core streaming business. The company confirmed to Lowpass it will no longer release new smart home devices beyond streaming-related products, while working through existing inventory. A spokesperson stated Roku will wind down hardware sales but provide continued support for current smart home products. Remaining items in stock include the Indoor Camera 360° ($49.99) and Video Doorbell & Chime ($89.99), both priced higher than their original launch prices of $39.99 and $79.99 respectively. The price increase aligns with Roku's July 2026 streaming device price hike. Other smart home products, including floodlights, solar panels, and smart plugs, are listed as out of stock. Roku has not disclosed details about ongoing support for existing users.

item.title: Google introduces Tabletop AI tool to streamline group planning
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Google Tabletop might be the fix we need for those never-ending group chat debates
Google Labs introduced Tabletop, an AI tool designed to streamline group planning by turning chat ideas into interactive tools. Announced on November 11, Tabletop allows users to create vacation itineraries, expense splitters, tournament brackets, and more without coding. By mentioning @tabletop or using templates, users generate shared spaces where collaborators can adjust plans in real time. Examples include interactive road trip maps with spinning wheels for meal choices and live pickleball brackets. The tool also features drag-and-drop seating charts for events. Available via a waitlist in the U.S. for users 18+, it aims to resolve planning disputes by automating decision-making. Google emphasizes flexibility, letting users modify tools as needs change. The product builds on prior AI app-building concepts but focuses on group collaboration. No pricing details were shared.
